snowflake.name: Stay on Snowflake
snowflake.summary: A cloud data warehouse that runs on AWS, Azure and Google Cloud.
snowflake.bestWhen: you share data between accounts, want AI functions in the warehouse, or run on three clouds.
snowflake.watchOut: credits cost more or less by edition and region, and the winner on cost can flip with your own numbers.

databricks.name: Databricks
databricks.summary: One platform for SQL, pipelines and model training, billed in Databricks Units.
databricks.bestWhen: code and machine learning matter as much as SQL.
databricks.watchOut: DBUs per hour by warehouse size were not on the sizing page we read, so check the vendor calculator, and managed Iceberg tables need Unity Catalog.

bigquery.name: Google BigQuery
bigquery.summary: A serverless warehouse on Google Cloud, billed per TiB scanned after a free first TiB each month.
bigquery.bestWhen: you already run on Google Cloud and want no servers to size.
bigquery.watchOut: on-demand billing follows bytes scanned, so a big query over a large table can cost a lot, and no self-hosting is stated.

redshift.name: Amazon Redshift
redshift.summary: A managed AWS warehouse that queries Iceberg tables in the Glue catalog.
redshift.bestWhen: your data and tools already sit in AWS.
redshift.watchOut: writing new Iceberg tables from Redshift itself is not stated, and AWS is phasing out Python user-defined functions after June 30, 2026.

fabric.name: Microsoft Fabric
fabric.summary: Microsoft's capacity-based analytics platform, built around OneLake.
fabric.bestWhen: Power BI is your main front end.
fabric.watchOut: its engines store Delta with Iceberg bridged by metadata, and capacities smaller than F64 need a licence per Power BI viewer.

clickhouse.name: ClickHouse
clickhouse.summary: A column-oriented database for fast scans, open source under Apache 2.0 or as a cloud service.
clickhouse.bestWhen: you have giant event tables and want dashboards that load fast.
clickhouse.watchOut: its Iceberg engine "may have limitations", and its docs list no full-fledged transactions.

motherduck.name: MotherDuck
motherduck.summary: A hosted version of DuckDB with a $0 Lite plan and a Business plan from $250 a month plus usage.
motherduck.bestWhen: a small team needs analytics fast and cheaply.
motherduck.watchOut: Lite caps internal users at 3 and Business at 10, and its Iceberg updates and deletes are merge-on-read only.

lakehouse.name: Dremio, Trino or Athena
lakehouse.summary: Query engines that read Iceberg tables in your own storage.
lakehouse.bestWhen: Iceberg tables in your own storage are the goal, or you ask occasional questions of files in S3.
lakehouse.watchOut: Athena and Trino list table-version limits, Dremio Enterprise has no published price, and SAP now owns Dremio.
